# mac-design

mac-design starts from one idea: Apple already designed your app, so pick the right system parts, arrange them, and stay out of their way, adding custom design only where the system has nothing. It applies Apple's eight principles as a review lens for every screen: Purpose, Agency, Responsibility, Familiarity, Flexibility, Simplicity, Craft, and Delight, with every screen answering where am I, what can I do, and where can I go. Before writing views, it asks for a design plan covering the archetype, information architecture with at most two sidebar levels, a command map, empty states, and the one feeling the app aims for. It designs small entry points first (global shortcut, menu bar, quick panel, drag and drop, Share menu), with optimistic UI and Undo rather than spinners. It sets layout rules for NavigationSplitView, spacing on a 4 pt grid, Liquid Glass only on the navigation and control layer, toolbar items placed over the column they act on, menus with shortcuts for every feature, calm window opening with no initial focus, keyboard-first interaction, system type and color, and dark mode as its own palette. Review is done when every rule in its design-rules reference holds on light and dark snapshots of every surface, or has a comment saying why not. Credit: created by daveebbelaar, in the bama repository. Source: https://github.com/daveebbelaar/bama, file skills/design/mac-design/SKILL.md.
